environment.shared_node_note: this node also serves a language model, so its load moves with someone else's work; the protocol interleaves configurations because on a node this noisy the per-configuration median is unreliable while the ratio between interleaved configurations is not

grids.benchmark_state: unforced multi-mode decay (nu=0.02, ZeroForcing) at amplitude 1, with an amplitude-1e-3 repeat to measure content-independence
grids.dealias_rank_ceiling_is: a WAVENUMBER (the largest k the 2/3 rule leaves resolved), not a mode count and not a rank; the dealiased NxN grid carries far more degrees of freedom than it (~1849 at N=64). The key name is historical and is kept because claims_registry.py verifies against it; D30.2 forbids expressing a rank as a multiple of it.
grids.protocol: interleaved: one round times the reference and every configuration once, so a slow patch of machine time inflates all of them together rather than whichever block happened to run during it

interpretation: Per-step cost is reported as a ratio against the pinned-thread full-grid reference under both accountings. No per-step speedup is claimed anywhere: the reduced method pays the same full-grid nonlinear evaluation as the reference plus its own factorization.

accountings.full_step: wall time of a complete reduced step, including the full-grid nonlinear evaluation and all projections
accountings.linear_algebra: measured time inside the whole-field SVD calls

method.benchmark_state: unforced multi-mode decay; the forced IC is not used because a fixed low rank on a forced field grows unboundedly and makes LAPACK fail, which is a property of that configuration and not of cost. An amplitude-1e-3 repeat measures the content-independence claim rather than assuming it.
method.rank_held_fixed: check_every is set beyond the run, so cost is measured at a fixed rank rather than under adaptation
method.why: the factorization is of the whole N x N field, so it is rank-independent and Theta(N^3); a linear-algebra win is not a per-step win

provenance.note: git_commit, driver_sha256 and driver_matches_HEAD are all captured at LAUNCH -- the commit that was HEAD when the process loaded its code, and the driver as it was then. driver_matches_HEAD compares that hash against the driver in that commit, and is what reproducible follows. An earlier version read HEAD and hashed the driver when the artifact was WRITTEN; for any run that outlasts a commit those were read together and the check compared the driver against itself, reporting true while the artifact recorded a driver the run never used. *_at_write and tree_moved_during_run are informational: a tree that moved during a run is a fact about the run, not a reason to discard the launch verdict. working_tree_dirty is recorded too, but a rewritten result file alone does not invalidate a run.
